pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows normal and 'urgent' rejected.
src/index.js item(); 'AC-2' test asserts exact labelled list.
'AC-3' test covers high, low, normal filters in id order.
'AC-4' test checks unfiltered list in id order.
'AC-5' test asserts exact nav markup for all four views.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty, __proto__; code uses a Set and has().
'AC-7' test asserts exact messages for no-match and empty table in all views. (The separate 'No match' state test was loosened, but AC-7 still covers the exact text.)
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; 'AC-8' test asserts it; the traffic checker was updated to allow queries.

findings.what: The last commit 'Follow-up edits' loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe('No low-priority items.') to toBeDefined(). message() returns a string or null, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec records no justification for loosening it.
The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened the 'No match' test to toBeDefined().
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or disclose and justify the loosening.

findings.what: The AC-8 test only checks that routes.json contains the string. Nothing shows the traffic worker requests the query path. The fake app change in test/traffic.test.js does allow checking this, but no test uses it with the real routes.
findings.fix: Optionally add a traffic test that asserts the round requests '/?priority=high'.

lenses.note: Spec present; the change matches its decisions. The traffic checker relaxation is a small addition, justified by AC-8.
All 8 items are implemented and named by tests. All four state rows have tests, but the No match test was weakened in the final commit.
npm test could not run here (vitest not installed). Judged by reading. One assertion can never fail (toBeDefined on message()).
README mentions the filter. The README does not mention the labels, which is minor.
The logic is correct. Invalid or empty priority gives 400, and queries are parameterized.
Priority is whitelisted and the SQL is bound. Titles are escaped. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and no screenshots were given.
No browser or preview is available, and the PR states none.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false (see finding).
